label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Topic: road
Claims (index: claim | suggested search):
0: Asphalt pavement is about 95 percent stone, sand and gravel bound by about 5 percent asphalt cement (bitumen) | asphalt pavement 95 percent aggregate 5 percent binder
1: Water in the base is the main enemy of a road; good drainage keeps the base strong | water in pavement base layer drainage road failure
2: A road is built in layers: compacted subgrade, a crushed stone base, then an asphalt surface | flexible pavement layers subgrade base course surface course

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
I searched each claim.

**Claim 0: asphalt pavement is about 95 percent stone, sand and gravel bound by about 5 percent asphalt cement. Supported as written (by weight).**
- National Academies (NCHRP): aggregate "typically makes up about 95% of an HMA mixture by weight, whereas asphalt binder makes up the remaining 5%." URL: https://nap.nationalacademies.org/read/14524/chapter/3
- GlobalSpec: hot mix asphalt "consists of 95% aggregate and 5% asphalt cement" and is used for over 90% of US roads. URL: https://www.globalspec.com/learnmore/building_construction/building_materials/asphalt_road_surfacing_materials
- FHWA: binder is approximately 5 to 6 percent by mass. URL: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/publications/research/infrastructure/structures/97148/app.cfm
- By volume it is about 85% aggregate, so the claim should say by weight or 'about 95 percent stone'.

**Claim 1: water in the base is the main enemy of a road; drainage keeps the base strong. Supported in a corrected form.**
- Missouri DOT pavement base study: inadequate drainage "has been identified as the most common cause" among the reasons cited for pavement failure. URL: https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/41188/dot_41188_DS1.pdf
- FHWA drainage guide: water enters and saturates the base; drainage systems reduce free water; positive drainage = permeable base + longitudinal edgedrain. URL: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/pavement/pubs/013241.pdf
- Corrected: "Poor drainage is one of the most common causes of road failure."

**Claim 2: a road is built in layers: subgrade, crushed stone base, asphalt surface. Supported as written.**
- Pavement Interactive: surface course on top, base course of aggregate or HMA below, optional subbase, then subgrade soil. URL: https://pavementinteractive.org/reference-desk/pavement-types-and-history/pavement-types/hma-pavement/
- Caltrans Highway Design Manual ch. 600 (pavement structure layers). URL: https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/programs/design/documents/chp0600-a11y.pdf
